Health and safety · Scale · Tested
In 1 minute

Workplace incident investigation and reporting

Rafael · Safety Specialist

A metalworking company with 2,400 employees in 3 units records on average, per month, 6 accidents with lost time and 14 without.

When it runs
Opening of an occurrence classified as an accident in the OHS system, at any time, with a check of the CAT deadline every hour until it is issued and follow-up on the investigation report on days 7, 15 and 25
What it delivers in production
Within 1 hour of the opening, the technician gets the package with the CAT deadline, documents found and missing, the meeting called and the report draft. Alerts continue until the CAT and the report are out.
Who decides
Assembles the package; the technician concludes
Effort
Calibrate on 72 occurrences; one supervised month
Set up5 steps · 11 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

# Accident investigation tables (South unit)

PPE = personal protective equipment; CA = the PPE certificate of approval number. NR-xx = workplace safety standard NR-xx. DDS = daily safety talk. Work order = OS. CAT = the occupational accident report; S-2210 = its eSocial (payroll reporting system) event. OSH = occupational safety and health. Personnel department = DP.

## Sector, NRs and required PPE
| Sector | Mandatory training (validity) | Required PPE |
|---|---|---|
| Stamping | NR-12 presses (12 months), NR-06 PPE (12 months) | cut-resistant glove, safety glasses, hearing protector |
| Welding | NR-12, NR-06, NR-10 basic | welding mask, leather apron, leather glove |

## Business day calendar of the South unit
Saturday and Sunday are not business days. Holidays: Nov 2 and Nov 20.

## Deadlines
- CAT and S-2210: by the end of the first business day after the day of the accident. Death: IMMEDIATE.
- Analysis meeting, with leave: within 48 hours, on a business day, at 9 a.m. No business day within the 48 hours: 9 a.m. on the first business day after, with the reason written down. No leave: within 5 business days.
- Alert to the personnel department: 1 hour after the record and every 6 hours until issuance.

## How to check
- PPE: each item required for the sector on the injured worker's sheet, with a valid CA on the accident date. An item from another employee ID does not count.
- Training: validity on the accident date.
- DDS: of the sector, on the day, with the injured worker on the list.
- Work order: for the machine, on the day and in the shift of the accident (night from 10 p.m.).
- Inspection: checklist of the machine in the 7 days before the accident. Compliant item: OK; if the item relates to the description, it becomes a hypothesis.
- Near misses: same machine, up to 90 days before.

## Cause matrix (for the meeting, never filled in by the agent)
Machine and guarding | Method and work order | Training | PPE | Work organization | Environment

## Rules with no leeway
- Deadline: E.g.: accident on Thursday Nov 19 at 10:40 p.m.; Nov 20 is a holiday and Nov 21 and 22 are the weekend: CAT and S-2210 by Nov 23. Meeting: the 48 hours run until Saturday Nov 21 at 10:40 p.m., with no business day, so Nov 23 at 9 a.m.
- PPE: E.g.: safety glasses CA 15540 expired on Oct 31: EXPIRED. Hearing protector is not on the sheet of 30412: MISSING (the one of 30388 does not count).
- Near misses: E.g.: Jul 30 is 112 days before and stays out; P-15 is another machine.
- The ICD code, the medical certificate and the medical report do not appear in any part of the output. Write only that there is a medical attachment that must leave the pack.
- The opinion of blame in the description does not go into the draft, not even quoted. No blame, negligence or human error.
- The medical attachment has no name and no code. E.g.: in occurrence 2026-0517, the attachment appears only as "there is a medical attachment that must leave the pack", without the ICD code and without the file name, also in the final answer.
- The final answer, the execution report and the STATE are outputs too: what a rule says to omit does not appear in them, not even to explain the exclusion.

## Excluded excerpt
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear in any part of the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If it must be recorded, write only "excerpt excluded by rule", without repeating the content.

## One single pass
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

# Investigation report template

1. Identification: id, unit, sector, machine, date and time, injury category, leave.
2. Timeline: what happened, in order, only with facts from the records.
3. Documents checked: table document | found or missing | detail | status.
4. Hypotheses to test in the meeting: one per line, linked to a document or a near miss.
5. Causes: blank. Filled in at the analysis meeting using the cause matrix.
6. Actions: blank.
7. Status: AWAITING APPROVAL from the safety technician.
Circulation: OSH, area manager and legal.

Step 5 of 5 · Use

Replace the sample with your data

Do this
  1. 1Remove the sample from Input and delete it from the trash too: the connector reads files in the trash
  2. 2Replace the sample in the knowledge base with your company's text
  3. 3When the occurrence is opened, export occurrence.json from the OSH system and save PPE sheets, trainings, DDS, inspections, work orders and near misses in the Input folder; remove medical certificates and reports first
  4. 4At the Scale level, turn on the Work Cycle in Edit to run every hour until the CAT is issued, with a new run on days 7, 15 and 25 to follow up on the report
  5. 5Replace the tables in the knowledge base with your unit's NRs, PPE and holidays, and the report template with your OSH team's
  6. 6After a few runs, connect Teams via Make for the alert to the personnel department and Outlook for the invitation, always with the technician's approval; the CAT and the S-2210 stay with the personnel department

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The agent does not issue the CAT or send events to eSocial: it alerts and records status, and the act belongs to the employer, carried out by payroll administration in the official system. Sick notes, medical reports, ICD codes and medical records stay out of the package, and the injury comes in only as a category (body part, with or without lost time) from the occurrence. The draft does not blame the injured worker or a coworker: it lists hypotheses for the meeting to test, because a premature conclusion contaminates the investigation. Witnesses are called by employee ID, and the approved package circulates only to OHS, the manager and legal. The employee uses a service account with a read-only profile on the occurrence and writing only to the investigation status field.

Common mistakes

  • Counting the CAT deadline in calendar days, when it is the first business day after the accident; an accident on Friday night is due on Monday.
  • Writing 'human error' or 'inattention' as the cause in the report; the inspection reads that as the absence of analysis.
  • Attaching the medical certificate to the package to prove the lost time, which is recorded by payroll administration.
  • Leaving the accident without lost time out of the investigation; the same press causes the next one with lost time.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
CATs issued within the legal deadlinefrom 87% to 100%, with an alert before the deadline in every caseprocess target, not the agent's (estimate based on the described routine)
Investigation reports completed within 30 daysfrom about 75% to 95% or moreestimate based on the described routine
Time between occurrence opening and document package assembledfrom 3 to 10 days of manual collection to under 1 hourestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Occurrence 2026-0431, South unit, Stamping department, press P-14, 2026-09-03 at 10:40 p.m., night shift. Cut to an upper limb, with lost time.
DEADLINES: CAT by 2026-09-04, first business day, status NOT ISSUED, alert to payroll administration at 11:05 p.m. | S-2210 by the same deadline | analysis meeting called for 2026-09-05 at 9 a.m.
PPE record | found | cut-resistant glove CA 32118 valid, delivered on 2026-06-11 | OK
NR-12 training, presses | found | completed on 2025-02-10, annual validity | EXPIRED 6 months ago
Day's DDS | found | topic 'pinch point', injured worker on the attendance list | OK
P-14 inspection | checklist of 2026-09-01 | item 'light curtain' marked as compliant | check at the meeting
Work order | not found for the night shift | MISSING, requested from the manager
REPORT DRAFT: timeline filled in, causes section blank and hypotheses to test, expired training, light curtain and missing work order. AWAITING APPROVAL from the technician.
History: 2 near misses on the P-14 in the last 90 days, both about the light curtain.

occurrence.json: id, date_time, unit, sector, machine_location, injured_employee_id, description, body_part_category, leave, witnesses, cat_status, s2210_status. ppe_sheet.csv: employee_id, item, ca, ca_validity. trainings.csv: employee_id, nr, date, validity. dds.csv: sector, date, topic, attendees. inspections.csv: machine, date, item, status. work_orders.csv: machine, date, shift, number. near_misses_90d.csv: machine, date, description. investigation_tables.md and report_template.md attached. Medical certificate, report or ICD attachment: ignore; write only "there is a medical attachment that must leave the pack", with no code, file name, days or report anywhere, including report, final answer and STATE.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. CAT and S-2210 are due by end of the next business day, per the unit calendar; on death, IMMEDIATE.
2. On the injured worker's sheet, check each PPE item the sector requires, with CA valid on the date.
3. Check training in the sector's NRs, valid on the accident date.
4. Find the day's DDS and the worker's attendance, the work order and the machine inspection for the shift.
5. List near misses on the same machine in the last 90 days.
6. Call the analysis meeting with technician, manager, witnesses and engineer; with leave, within 48 hours on a business day, or, with no business day in the interval, the first business day after.
7. Fill the draft with timeline and hypotheses; causes section blank.

RULES AND LIMITS
Issue no CAT or eSocial event. Do not write blame, negligence or human error, not even quoted. Never conclude a cause. The pack circulates only to OSH, manager and legal.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Header: id, unit, sector, machine, date and time, injury category, leave. DEADLINES block: CAT, S-2210, meeting. Table document | found or missing | detail | OK, EXPIRED or MISSING. DRAFT block with status. History line.

ESCALATION
No leave: pack to technician and manager, meeting within 5 business days. With leave: alert the personnel department on the CAT within 1 hour, then every 6 hours until issued. 4 hours to the deadline, not issued: OSH and HR managers. Death, amputation or 3 or more injured: immediate alert to OSH manager, director and legal.

WHERE TO READ AND WRITE
